1.explanation:
1. rules/constructor-super.md – Documents exactly the logic that checks for valid super() calls; this is where ESLint tracks the superCalled flag that is throwing an undefined-property error.
2. rules/no-this-before-super.md – Explains the complementary rule that must coordinate with constructor-super to prevent use of this before super; often these two rules share internal state and initialization logic.
3. developer-guide/working-with-rules.md – Gives an overview of how visitor patterns and rule contexts operate, useful for understanding why the rule context might be undefined.
4. developer-guide/code-path-analysis.md – Details how ESLint traverses the AST and maintains state across function and class constructors; essential for reproducing the break in state tracking.
5. developer-guide/source-code.md – Provides a map of the project’s code layout so you can locate the implementation files (lib/rules/constructor-super.js, etc.) and understand the broader architecture.
6. developer-guide/unit-tests.md – Shows how rule tests are written and run; useful for creating a minimal test case that reproduces the superCalled error in CI or locally.
1.bug_scenario: In the screenshot we see VS Code with the ESLint extension reporting a runtime exception inside ESLint (‘Cannot read property “superCalled” of undefined’) with a red error banner at the top. In the editor window there’s a simple ES2015 class definition (class Extender, class BugProof extends Extender), a constructor that calls super(props), and a try/catch around an empty for…of loop. As soon as the user types an extra blank line at the end (line 21), ESLint crashes, reporting a parsing error at that last line while internally trying to read “superCalled” on an undefined object. The bug involves the constructor-super rule (and internally its tracking of whether super() has been called), the parsing logic, and the way ESLint’s rule engine tracks state for each constructor node.
